title: Laboratory & radiology
summary: Order → pay → barcoded sample → scanner-first result grid → verification → publish to doctor; PACS linking.
markdown:
# Laboratory & radiology

The quality side of both departments (the patient identified at collection and before an examination, rejected samples,
samples sent to partner laboratories, turnaround and its MSDS score, critical results, the radiologist's report,
outsourced examinations, repeats, the written policies) is in [diagnostic services quality](diagnostic-services.md).

## Lab: the 5 steps (§4.1) + verification (§4.5)

1. **Order** — doctor: `POST /lab/requisitions {"ticket_id": 42, "test_ids": [1, 3], "priority": "STAT"}`
   (inpatients: `admission_id` → billed to the running bill). One sample with a unique barcode
   (`LB-2026-0000123`) is created per test. OPD orders create a finalized **Lab invoice**.
   The order is written in the consultation or the inpatient's chart: send that visit's `ticket_id`, or the stay's
   `admission_id` for an inpatient.
2. **Pay** — at reception/cashier: `POST /finance/invoices/{invoice_id}/payments` (lab staff never take
   cash; `LAB_PAYMENT_REQUIRED` until paid — IPD and Emergency are exempt).
3. **Collect & label** — `POST /lab/samples/{sample_id}/collect {"wristband_code": "…"}` (or
   `{"identity_check": "TwoIdentifiers"}`: the patient is identified first, MSDS AAC 3) → label print payload (50 mm
   label printer). Ward and ER nurses collect at the bedside too. An unusable sample:
   `POST /lab/samples/{sample_id}/reject {"code": "Haemolysed"}` (a new sample to collect). A jammed or smudged label:
   `GET /lab/samples/{sample_id}/label` prints it again. Call it only when the user prints, never for a preview: each
   call is one more label (`label_print_count` in `GET /lab/scan/{barcode}`), whether or not the printer printed it,
   and is logged as a PHI access. It never changes the sample, so its `row_version` stays (decisions 53).
4. **Scan & enter** — bench scanner: `GET /lab/scan/{barcode}` → `metric_grid` with this patient's
   reference ranges (male/female/default) and critical limits. Flag values live. Then
   `POST /lab/items/{item_id}/results {"metrics": {"hb": 6.5, "wbc": 12.2}, "interpretation": "…"}` —
   result is `PendingVerification`, reagents are deducted by the test's bill of materials (FEFO) and
   verifiers get `lab.result.pending_verification`, and so does every bench (`lab.result.enter`): refresh the
   worklist. `POST /lab/samples/{sample_id}/receive` first starts the turnaround clock (`due_at` on the worklist).
5. **Verify & publish** — `GET /lab/verification-queue` (critical first) →
   `POST /lab/results/{id}/verify {"decision": "Verified"}` → `Published`; the ordering doctor gets
   `lab.result.published` + an inbox notification. A lab-only walk-in has no ordering doctor: its publication goes to
   the reception desk that registers walk-ins instead ([OPD reception](opd-reception.md), §6). The bench does not get
   it. `Rejected` (note required) sends it back to the bench.
   The person who entered a result cannot verify it (`LAB_VERIFIER_MUST_DIFFER`). A critical result opens the critical
   results log: tell the doctor now and record it (`POST /critical-results/{id}/communications`).
   Each queue row carries its context, so the verifier's screen needs no other read and never matches names:
   `requisition_id` and `requisition_number` (open the order with `GET /lab/requisitions/{requisition_id}`),
   `patient_id`, the sample's `barcode`, `entered_by` (the user who entered it: compare it with the signed-in user's id
   to warn before `LAB_VERIFIER_MUST_DIFFER`) and `due_at` with `is_overdue` (ask for the optional `delay_reason` before
   verifying; a correction is never overdue). **A lost verify answer:** never repeat the decision by itself. Read
   `GET /lab/requisitions/{requisition_id}` and find the `result_id` in `results`: `Published` (with `verified_stamp`)
   or `Rejected` is decided; still `PendingVerification`, offer it again. A row gone from the queue says neither
   (backend issue #29).

Doctors only ever see published results: `GET /lab/requisitions/{id}`,
`GET /lab/patients/{patient_id}/results?test_id=` (trend charts). Each result carries who performed it
(`performed_stamp`) and who verified it (`verified_stamp`): name, designation, registration, date-time (MSDS 147).

**Critical values** (audit F-23) — when a critical value is entered, the verifiers and the ordering doctor get
`lab.result.critical_pending` (`release_after_minutes`): verifiers check critical values first. The one exception to
"published only": a critical value still unverified after the setting `lab_critical_release_minutes` (default 15) is
shown to the ordering doctor, with `status: "PendingVerification"` and `provisionally_released_at` set, in
`GET /lab/requisitions/{id}` and `GET /lab/patients/{patient_id}/results`, announced by `lab.result.provisional` and an
inbox notification. Show it in red as "Pending verification" and never print it (the lab report prints published
results only). If the verifier rejects it, `lab.result.provisional_withdrawn`: the doctor must not act on it. The
critical results log still opens when the value is published.

**The lab report** — `GET /lab/requisitions/{id}/report/print-payload` (A4) or its `pdf_url`
(`GET /lab/requisitions/{id}/report/pdf`), for the doctor, the ward or the reception desk handing reports to
walk-in patients: the published tests, each metric with the reference range for the patient's sex and its flag, the
interpretation, an amended result's reason, and under each test the technician's and the verifier's stamps.
`complete: false` = some tests are still in the lab (the report says it is partial); nothing verified yet →
`LAB_REPORT_NOT_READY`.

**Cancelling an order** — before any of its tests is sampled: `POST /lab/requisitions/{requisition_id}/cancel
{"reason": "..."}` cancels the tests and voids an unpaid lab bill. The doctor who ordered it cancels their own order;
the lab admin any order (another doctor's: `FORBIDDEN`). Once a sample is collected the order stays
(`LAB_ITEM_STATE_INVALID`): an unusable sample is rejected on the bench instead.

**Re-runs** — `POST /lab/items/{item_id}/rerun {"reason"}` creates a linked re-run item with a new
barcode, not billed again; its reagent usage is flagged `is_rerun` (abuse is swept).
**Corrections** — `POST /lab/items/{item_id}/corrections` amends a published result; it is re-verified
and then supersedes the original.

## Lab admin (§4.3)

Tests & metric schemas (`POST /lab/tests`), prices (`PUT /lab/tests/{id}/price`, Lab Admin only;
existing orders keep their price), reagents & batches, BOM (`PUT /lab/tests/{id}/bom`),
write-offs, `GET /lab/dashboard` (revenue − reagent COGS = net, contractor/hospital share). A contracted laboratory:
`PUT /lab/contractor {"hospital_share_pct", "contractor_employee_id"}`, the contractor picked with
`GET /staff/lookup?q=`; a contracting firm instead: `contractor_vendor_id` from `GET /finance/vendors`.
Missing BOM → result submission refused (`LAB_REAGENT_BOM_MISSING`) or flagged, per hospital policy.
A send-out test's partner from `GET /diagnostic-partners`, a reagent batch's supplier invoice from
`GET /pharmacy-admin/vendor-invoices`, and the batch of a write-off (`POST /lab/reagent-adjustments`) from
`GET /lab/reagents/{reagent_id}/batches`: the batches still in stock, the first to expire first, with what is left
(`qty_available`); an expired one (`is_expired`) is written off with reason `Expiry`.

## Radiology / PACS (§4.6)

1. Doctor: `POST /imaging/orders {"ticket_id", "modality": "XRay", "body_part": "Chest PA", "laterality",
   "service_id"}` → returns `accession_number` (≤ 16 chars) — the modality must use it.
   The order is written in the consultation or the inpatient's chart (that visit's `ticket_id`, or the stay's
   `admission_id`); the service from `GET /finance/service-catalog?category=Imaging`.
2. Radiographer: `GET /imaging/worklist`, `POST /imaging/orders/{id}/status`: `InProgress` records the checks before the
   examination (the patient identified, `site_confirmed`, `pregnancy_status` when needed), `Completed` the contrast
   and the doctor present (`contrast_doctor_id`: the `employee_id` from `GET /staff/lookup?q=…&license_type=PMDC`).
3. Link the study: `POST /imaging/orders/{id}/link-study` with `{}` (auto-find in Orthanc by accession) or
   `{"orthanc_study_id"}` copied from the PACS (the server checks it there and takes the study's UID from the PACS).
   The worker also auto-links every 2 minutes; a study linked while the examination is in progress
   completes it. A server without PACS answers `PACS_NOT_CONFIGURED` (never retry: the examination ends with status
   `Completed`, the report works without images); `ORTHANC_UNAVAILABLE`: the PACS did not answer (retryable);
   `IMAGING_STUDY_NOT_FOUND`: not in the PACS yet. Doctor gets `imaging.study.available`
   with `viewer_url` (Stone / OHIF / Orthanc Explorer 2) — open it in a separate window. `viewer_url` is null when
   IT has set no viewer address (`ORTHANC_PUBLIC_URL`): show the study as linked, without *Open images*.
4. Report (a radiologist: PMDC and the RadiologyReporting privilege): `POST /imaging/orders/{id}/report {"report_text",
   "critical_finding_id"}` → `imaging.report.ready`. The report is final; it
   carries the reporter's stamp (`reported_stamp` of `GET /imaging/orders/{id}`); a critical finding opens the critical
   results log.
5. Print: `GET /imaging/orders/{id}/report/print-payload` (A4: study, clinical indication, report, stamp) or its
   `pdf_url` (`GET /imaging/orders/{id}/report/pdf`); not reported yet → `IMAGING_REPORT_NOT_READY`.
